              "file": "source/text.md",
              "line": 25,
              "quote": "Sample Pyrolysis Procedures. First, pyrolysis characteristics of cathode and anode materials were, respectively, analyzed by TG-GC/ MS which included a thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA) (Labsys Evo1600, France), auto injector system (Automation Autoinjector Corp., Italy), and GC/MS (TRACE GC Ultra/ISQ Single Quadrupole MS, USA). TG tests were first conducted to analyze the decomposition process of organics in raw LiCoO and graphite particles, and then, pyrolysis products at weight loss temperature were collected and injected into the GC/MS system by an auto injector system. Pyrolysis experiments of electrode material mixtures were conducted in a controlled atmosphere tube furnace (MXG1200-80, Shanghai Micro-X furnace Co., Ltd.). In each experiment, the 5 g sample was placed into the corundum tube and the tube was sealed by flanges at both ends. A vacuum pump was first applied to provide the vacuum environment, and then, the corundum tube was filled with high purity nitrogen with the gas flow of 200 mL/min. Gas pyrolysis products could be taken out of the tube by nitrogen flow, and then, macromolecular organics could be collected by condensation while small molecule organic gases were treated by a gas-treating system. Pyrolysis temperature increased from an initial temperature of ∴ _ 30 to a terminal temperature of 500 ^∘C at a heating rate of 10 ^∘C / m i n. Samples would be processed at an isothermal temperature of 500 °C for 30 min. Afterward, the samples were naturally cooled to 30 ^∘C in a nitrogen atmosphere. After pyrolysis, a part of the pyrolytic electrode material was treated by ultrasound at solid/liquid ratio of 1:10 g/mL with an ultrasonic frequency of 25 kHz and electric power of 800 W for 2 h. Afterward, electrode materials were separated by the filtration method and dried at 80 ^∘C. By these processes, three samples were prepared for flotation: raw electrode material mixture (REM), pyrolytic electrode material mixture (PEM), and pyrolysis-ultrasonic pretreated electrode material mixture (PUEM)."

              "quote": "On the basis of the TG analysis, the pyrolysis products of electrode materials at temperatures of 120 and 500 ^∘C were sampled via the auto injector system that was connected with the GC and TGA system, and gas analysis was conducted in the GC/MS system. Figure 4 demonstrates that pyrolysis products at a pyrolysis temperature of 120 ^∘C come from ester electrolyte, such as dimethyl carbonate, ethylene carbonate, and propylene carbonate. Organic pyrolysis products at a pyrolysis temperature of 500 ^∘C are mostly fluorides that mainly come from the decomposition of PVDF, such as vinylidene fluoride, 1,3,5-trifluorobenzene, 1,4-difluoroben zene, ^1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 -hexafluoro-propane, and 1,2,4-trifluoroben zene, which demonstrates that PVDF has been decomposed at a pyrolysis temperature of 500 ^∘C. In the pyrolysis process, a part of the polymer structure o - (CH2 - CF2) - n decomposes to a single molecule of CH2 = CF2 while others separate out HF and their carbon chain fracture to form small molecules. Ethylene carbonate and propylene carbonate are from residual electrolyte. These results demonstrate that the main organics in electrode materials are organic binder and electrolyte and pyrolysis can effectively remove organic binder and electrolyte."

              "line": 25,
              "quote": "Sample Pyrolysis Procedures. First, pyrolysis characteristics of cathode and anode materials were, respectively, analyzed by TG-GC/ MS which included a thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA) (Labsys Evo1600, France), auto injector system (Automation Autoinjector Corp., Italy), and GC/MS (TRACE GC Ultra/ISQ Single Quadrupole MS, USA). TG tests were first conducted to analyze the decomposition process of organics in raw LiCoO and graphite particles, and then, pyrolysis products at weight loss temperature were collected and injected into the GC/MS system by an auto injector system. Pyrolysis experiments of electrode material mixtures were conducted in a controlled atmosphere tube furnace (MXG1200-80, Shanghai Micro-X furnace Co., Ltd.). In each experiment, the 5 g sample was placed into the corundum tube and the tube was sealed by flanges at both ends. A vacuum pump was first applied to provide the vacuum environment, and then, the corundum tube was filled with high purity nitrogen with the gas flow of 200 mL/min. Gas pyrolysis products could be taken out of the tube by nitrogen flow, and then, macromolecular organics could be collected by condensation while small molecule organic gases were treated by a gas-treating system. Pyrolysis temperature increased from an initial temperature of ∴ _ 30 to a terminal temperature of 500 ^∘C at a heating rate of 10 ^∘C / m i n. Samples would be processed at an isothermal temperature of 500 °C for 30 min. Afterward, the samples were naturally cooled to 30 ^∘C in a nitrogen atmosphere. After pyrolysis, a part of the pyrolytic electrode material was treated by ultrasound at solid/liquid ratio of 1:10 g/mL with an ultrasonic frequency of 25 kHz and electric power of 800 W for 2 h. Afterward, electrode materials were separated by the filtration method and dried at 80 ^∘C. By these processes, three samples were prepared for flotation: raw electrode material mixture (REM), pyrolytic electrode material mixture (PEM), and pyrolysis-ultrasonic pretreated electrode material mixture (PUEM)."
